regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY flatters. Decompose it: IIP overall came in at 6.7% YoY, down from 8.8%, while core sector moderated to 5.4% YoY from 6.0%. The PMI composite at 54.6 is services-led — manufacturing PMI slipped to 52.8 from 53.5. The inversion: capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is rising, which should pull private capex forward — but credit card growth at just 2.3% YoY suggests the mass consumer is not participating in the headline story.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY is above the 4% midpoint, but the real problem is the composition. Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY — a 95th-percentile print — is feeding into WPI at 9.92% YoY, which will transmit to core CPI with a 2-quarter lag. Core CPI is already at 3.9% YoY and rising. The RBI's own inflation forecast has been revised up to 5.1% YoY from 4.6% — the committee is telling you a cut is off the table, even as the growth narrative softens.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% YoY — a 630 bps divergence — has pushed the CD ratio to 81.4%, the 75th percentile historically. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% while the repo rate was being held was FY14; within 12 months, the taper tantrum forced an emergency reversal. Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month sits at the 0th percentile — capital markets are not providing the relief valve. NBFC credit accelerating to 14.9% YoY from 10.6% signals wholesale funding pressure is building, not easing.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate is being compressed by rising inflation — RBI's own forecast of 5.1% YoY puts the real repo rate near zero. At INR 96.15 and US 10Y at 5.22% yield, the carry differential is insufficient to attract sustained FII debt flows. The RBI is simultaneously managing currency depreciation, inflation overshoot, and a credit-deposit imbalance — three objectives, one instrument. Something will give, and the sequencing matters enormously for housing affordability and corporate capex IRRs.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation rising to 77.4% of capacity — up from 75.6% — is the most credible signal of a genuine investment upcycle. Credit to industry surged to 20.0% YoY from 6.5%, and credit to services to 22.9% YoY from 10.2%, confirming that financing is flowing to productive capacity. The inversion: core sector growth moderated to 5.4% YoY from 6.0%, and cement and steel — the physical proof of capex — are not yet confirming the financial flows. Watch whether capacity utilisation crosses 80% before declaring the cycle self-sustaining.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month is a strong print, but the question is: how much is genuine demand versus formalization reclassifying existing spend? Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler at 19.7% YoY suggest the formal economy is spending. But credit card growth at 2.3% YoY — down from 5.6% — signals that mass-market revolving credit is contracting. The divergence: affluent urban consumers are buying cars and SIPs; the mass consumer is deleveraging. GST's headline flatters a bifurcated demand picture.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 350 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (latest, down from 82.5% prior month) remains elevated at 75th percentile historically. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened for 3 consecutive months. NBFC credit growth accelerating at 14.9% YoY (latest, up from 10.6% YoY prior) signals wholesale funding pressure. Corporate bond issuance at 18,700 ₹ cr / month (latest) at historical lows (0th percentile), indicating capital markets are not absorbing the overflow.","implication":"RBI will face pressure to either tighten liquidity or signal deposit-friendly measures within 2-3 months. Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; their cost of funds will spike. Position for a potential RBI liquidity injection or a credit growth slowdown if deposits don't accelerate.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile is historically tight. The last time it was this elevated (2022-23), RBI tightened policy and credit growth decelerated sharply within 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY (latest) signals robust investment demand. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (latest, up from 75.6% prior month) — rising for 2 consecutive months and at 74th percentile. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (latest, down from 6.0% prior) shows some moderation but remains positive. Credit to industry at 20.0% YoY (latest, up from 6.5% prior) and credit to services at 22.9% YoY (latest, up from 10.2% prior) confirm broad-based capex financing. PMI composite at 54.6 index (latest, up from 54.3 prior) at 83rd percentile — highest in 10 years.","implication":"Capex cycle is self-reinforcing: rising capacity utilisation → higher capex orders → credit growth to industry accelerating. Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks. Increase exposure to project-linked financials (IL&FS, NBCC). Expect order book visibility to extend 12-18 months. Risk: if credit tightens (see Sig1), capex financing could stall — hedge with puts on discretionary capex plays.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is near the 10-year median and signals healthy demand. Historically, when CU exceeds 78%, capex accelerates but inflation risks rise — we're at the inflection point.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit Record; Affluent Money Entering","data_text":"SIP inflows at 32,297 ₹ cr / month (latest, up from 31,961 ₹ cr / month prior) — rising 2 consecutive months and at 92nd percentile. SIP accounts at 100.18 mn (latest, up from 99.06 mn prior) at 82nd percentile. SIP AUM at 18.62 ₹ lakh cr (latest, up from 18.21 ₹ lakh cr prior) — rising 2 consecutive months and at 93rd percentile. Critically: SIP AUM growing 2.3% MoM while SIP accounts growing 1.1% MoM — average ticket size per account rising, indicating affluent retail entering. DII equity net at 58,502 ₹ cr net / month (latest, up from 35,099 ₹ cr net / month prior) at 100th percentile — domestic institutions in full accumulation mode. MF AUM at 87.08 ₹ lakh cr (latest, up from 85.76 ₹ lakh cr prior) at 86th percentile.","implication":"Retail equity participation is broadening upmarket — this is late-cycle behaviour. Allocate to large-cap quality and dividend-paying stocks; avoid micro-cap momentum plays. SIP inflows provide a structural bid under equity markets, but rising ticket sizes suggest retail is chasing returns. Reduce leverage in portfolios; position for volatility. Watch for SIP growth rate to decelerate — when it does, equity flows will reverse sharply.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile are near all-time highs. Historically, when SIP inflows peak, equity market corrections follow within 3-6 months as retail capitulates.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI's Comfort","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest, up from 20.05% YoY prior) — at 95th percentile, the highest in the 10-year distribution. Brent crude at 105.47 $/bbl (latest, flat) and WTI at 92.6 $/bbl (latest, flat) — both at 73rd and 78th percentiles respectively. Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY (latest, up from 4.38% YoY prior) and core CPI at 3.9% YoY (latest) — both rising. RBI's inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY (latest, up from 4.6% YoY prior) signals RBI expects further overshoot. FAO food index at 130.3 index (latest, up from 129.7 prior) — rising but not alarming. India's import bill for oil at elevated levels; INR depreciation (see Sig6) amplifies rupee cost of crude.","implication":"RBI will struggle to cut rates in 2026 if fuel inflation persists above 20% YoY. Repo rate at 5.25% p.a. (latest, flat) is likely to remain on hold for 2-3 quarters. Hedge inflation exposure via TIPS, inflation-linked bonds, or commodity-linked equities (oil & gas, fertiliser). Reduce duration in fixed income — long-dated bonds will underperform. Monitor geopolitical risk (Middle East, Russia) for oil supply shocks.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is extreme. The last time fuel inflation exceeded 20% YoY (2021-22), RBI hiked rates aggressively and growth decelerated.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"Fed Tightening Cycle Resumes; Carry Unwind Risk","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (latest, up from 3.63% p.a. prior) — rising 2 in a row and at 68th percentile. US 10-year Treasury yield at 5.22% yield (latest, down from 5.28% prior) but at 95th percentile historically — near all-time highs. US core CPI at 2.45% YoY (latest, down from 2.47% prior) — falling 2 in a row, but core PCE at 3.01% YoY (latest, up from 2.98% prior) — rising. BOJ rate at 1.0% p.a. (latest, up from 0.75% p.a. prior) — at 86th percentile, signalling tightening. ECB deposit rate at 2.25% p.a. (latest, up from 2.0% prior). US PMI composite at 56.0 index (latest, up from 54.5 prior) at 84th percentile — US economy resilient. DXY at 102.406 index (latest, flat) at 56th percentile — dollar stable but elevated.","implication":"Fed tightening cycle is resuming; carry trades (long INR, long emerging market assets funded in USD) face unwind risk. FII equity net at 29,631 ₹ cr net / month (latest, up from 20,200 ₹ cr net / month prior) is at 83rd percentile but vulnerable to reversal if US yields spike further. Reduce leverage in EM portfolios. Hedge USD exposure via forwards or options. Watch for a break above 5.30% in US 10-year yields — that would trigger a sharp EM outflow.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"US 10-year Treasury yield at 95th percentile is historically restrictive. The last time yields were this high (2023), EM currencies depreciated sharply and equity flows reversed.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Depreciation Accelerates; RBI Intervention Likely","data_text":"INR/USD at 96.15 ₹ (latest, up from 95.76 ₹ prior) — at 91st percentile, near all-time weakness. INR has depreciated 4 of last 5 observations, signalling sustained selling pressure. FII equity net at 29,631 ₹ cr net / month (latest, up from 20,200 ₹ cr net / month prior) is positive but volatile — recent: -114 → -3,111.9 → 29,631 ₹ cr net / month shows sharp reversals. India's current account deficit is widening due to elevated oil imports (fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY) and weak commodity exports. RBI repo rate at 5.25% p.a. (latest, flat) is not high enough to attract carry flows if US yields remain above 5.2%.","implication":"RBI will likely intervene to defend INR, either via spot sales or forward guidance. Expect INR to trade in a 95.5–97.5 ₹/USD range over next 2 quarters. Corporates with USD liabilities should hedge; those with USD receivables should delay conversion. Avoid long INR positions unless paired with high-yielding rupee assets. Monitor RBI's FX reserve adequacy — if reserves fall below $600 bn, RBI may tighten liquidity further, pressuring credit growth.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 96.15 is at 91st percentile weakness. Historically, when INR weakens this sharply, RBI intervenes and equity markets correct 5-10% as liquidity tightens.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Shift, Not IT Weakness","data_text":"Office absorption at 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter (latest, up from 11.2 mn sq ft / quarter prior) appears strong at 7th percentile, but the trend is deceptive: recent: 21 → 13.2 → 21 → 13.2 → 4.02 → 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter shows violent oscillation with a 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter trough 2 observations ago. Office vacancy at 14.5% vacant (latest, down from 16.1% prior) — improving, but this masks a structural shift. Nifty IT index is flat (Nifty 23,447 at 72nd percentile) despite office absorption recovering, whereas retail mall vacancy at 4.8% vacant (latest, down from 5.0% prior) is at 7th percentile — tightest in 10 years. Rent in Bengaluru at 100.6 ₹/sqft/mo (latest, up from 94 ₹/sqft/mo prior) and Mumbai at 168.6 ₹/sqft/mo (latest, up from 159 ₹/sqft/mo prior) — both rising, but office rents are not accelerating as fast as retail rents.","implication":"Global Capability Centers (GCCs) — captive R&D and engineering hubs of multinational corporates — are the primary office absorbers, NOT traditional IT services firms. This decouples office RE from IT services stock performance. Overweight commercial real estate plays (Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield REITs) and underweight IT services stocks — the office cycle is driven by GCC capex, not IT headcount. Retail mall recovery (vacancy at 7th percentile) is the real story; e-commerce GMV growth at 18% YoY (latest) is slowing, suggesting brick-and-mortar is recapturing share. Position for a retail RE rerating and IT services multiple compression.","pct_10y":7,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 7th percentile is historically weak, but the composition has shifted from IT services to GCCs. This is a structural reallocation of real estate demand that equity markets have not yet priced in.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Services Carry Growth — Mass Consumer Quietly Steps Back

The facts:

  • PMI Composite at 54.6 index (83rd percentile) is services-driven — PMI Manufacturing slipped to 52.8 from 53.5 even as the composite rose.
  • IIP YoY decelerated to 6.7% YoY from 8.8%; core sector moderated to 5.4% YoY from 6.0% — the physical economy is not matching the financial narrative.
  • Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY signal affluent and aspirational demand is intact.
  • But credit card growth collapsed to 2.3% YoY from 5.6% — the mass consumer is deleveraging, not spending.

The tension: GDP at 7.8% YoY and GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month suggest broad-based strength; credit card contraction and manufacturing PMI slippage suggest the load is carried by the top quartile of consumers, not the economy as a whole.

Bottom line: Watch two-wheeler sales as the mass-market proxy — a deceleration below 15% YoY would confirm the bifurcation is widening, not narrowing.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US Resilience Exports Tightening — China Cannot Offset

The facts:

  • US PMI Composite at 56.0 index (84th percentile) keeps the Fed on hold; Fed Funds at 3.75% p.a. rose for the second consecutive observation.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.22% yield (95th percentile) — even after easing from 5.28% — is doing the tightening the Fed has not formally announced.
  • China GDP decelerated to 4.3% YoY from 5.0%; PMI Composite at 49.5 index signals contraction — no commodity reflation rescue from Beijing.
  • BOJ at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile, up from 0.75%) is unwinding the last major carry trade anchor; yen volatility transmits to EM within 60–90 days.

The tension: US growth surveys signal re-acceleration, but US GDP SAAR at 2.2% is decelerating and real tightening is embedded in 5.22% 10Y yields. China's weakness prevents commodity prices from sustaining — Brent flat at $105/bbl despite four consecutive up-sessions is the tell.

Bottom line: BOJ normalisation is the underpriced tail risk for India liquidity — watch the yen cross; a move through 140 ¥/$ accelerates EM carry unwinds.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Flood, Structural Drought — SIPs vs Deposit Gap

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (92nd percentile) — rising for two consecutive months; SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (93rd percentile) growing 2.3% MoM vs accounts growing 1.1% MoM, signalling ticket-size inflation as affluent retail enters.
  • DII equity net at ₹58,502 cr net / month (100th percentile) — domestic institutions in full accumulation; FII equity net at ₹29,631 cr net / month positive but volatile (prior two prints: -₹114 cr, -₹3,112 cr net / month).
  • But deposit growth at 10.8% YoY against credit at 17.1% YoY leaves the banking system structurally short of stable funding.
  • Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month (0th percentile) — capital markets are not absorbing the overflow from the banking system.

The tension: Equity liquidity is abundant — SIPs and DIIs are at multi-year highs. Banking system liquidity is structurally stressed — the CD ratio at 81.4% and bond market at a 10-year low in issuance means credit growth is being funded by increasingly thin deposit margins.

Bottom line: If deposit growth does not accelerate to close the gap with credit within two quarters, watch for RBI macro-prudential action on risk weights — the playbook from FY23 unsecured lending is the template.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Retail Tightest in a Decade; Office Oscillates — REITs Mispriced

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up 5 pp vs prior period); NRI share within premium/luxury at 25%; remittances at $140 bn (12.8% YoY) provide the funding base.
  • Retail mall vacancy at 4.8% vacant (7th percentile, tightest in 10 years) — Hyderabad and Bengaluru lead residential sales at 15% YoY and 12% YoY respectively; NCR sales turned negative at -1% YoY.
  • Office absorption at 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter (7th percentile) masks violent oscillation — the prior five prints: 21 → 13.2 → 21 → 13.2 → 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter; GCC now 41% of occupier mix, displacing IT services at 15%.
  • But Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, and Brookfield at ₹263/unit are all down sharply from prior levels — the market is pricing office uncertainty that retail vacancy data does not support.

The tension: Retail real estate is at a structural vacancy low; office absorption is oscillating at a structural low. REITs — which are predominantly office — are being sold as if both are weak. The divergence between retail tightness and office volatility is not yet reflected in REIT pricing.

Bottom line: Retail-heavy REIT exposure is underpriced relative to vacancy fundamentals; avoid pure-play office REITs until GCC demand stabilises above 14 mn sq ft / quarter for two consecutive prints.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Fuses, One Spark — Ranked by Probability × Impact

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent at $105/bbl — every $10 adds ~$15 bn to India's import bill, widens CAD ~40 bps, and feeds back into CPI with a 2-quarter lag; RBI's own forecast already at 5.1% YoY.
  • CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile) with corporate bond issuance at a 10-year low — if deposit growth does not recover, NBFC funding costs rise and the credit upcycle stalls before private capex confirms.
  • INR at 96.15 ₹ (91st percentile) with US 10Y at 5.22% yield — the carry differential is insufficient; FII equity flows reversed twice in the last three months and a third reversal would pressure RBI reserves.
  • BOJ at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile) — yen carry unwind is the least-priced global tail risk; prior BOJ moves at this percentile have transmitted to EM within 60–90 days.

The tension: All four risks are connected: oil widens CAD, CAD pressures INR, INR weakness amplifies oil's rupee cost, and a BOJ shock could trigger the FII reversal that turns a managed depreciation into a disorderly one.

Bottom line: Watch RBI's inflation forecast at the next policy meeting — if it is revised above 5.5% YoY, the rate-cut narrative collapses and Bank Nifty at the 90th percentile becomes the most exposed index.

"}
